purpose: Define source-faithful classification and plugin ownership before per-node transcription. This is not accepted semantic authority.
invariants: no source construct may be silently dropped
legacy ID, SortKey, XML position, or display order is not canonical identity
source parsing does not grant canonical or runtime authority
prose extraction is proposal or unresolved until explicitly accepted
target-specific interaction is not business action meaning
function-level potential CRUD is not business-action-specific CRUD
native script effect is not inferred solely from declared CRUD
new semantic requirements are plugin/extension-first; legacy schema names do not become Core kinds by default
legacy TableKey, Relationship key mapping, and Function selection key are distinct source facts and are not business occurrence identity by themselves
a legacy PK/SK declaration or key-field correspondence does not establish an accepted functional dependency without explicit semantic acceptance or corroborating evidence

sourceLocator.exactSnapshot: artifact digest + XML structural path + sibling ordinal + available legacy attributes
sourceLocator.semantics: source locator is stable only within the exact source artifact and is never canonical identity
sourceLocator.crossRevision: reconcile through accepted semantic identity or explicit migration mapping; do not match by SortKey alone

candidateExtensions.responsibility: Parse Xead/Xeaf losslessly enough to inventory known and unknown constructs, preserve source locators, and emit transcription candidates.
Carry X-TEA-specific relational semantics only where existing TEI Data/Relation meaning is not lossless, including legacy relation taxonomy and conditional existence.
Represent subsystem grouping, ownership pressure, and cross-subsystem operation diagnostics without making Subsystem a Core kind.
Represent design Function, I/O and call relations as a review lens over Application Pattern, Query, Capability and Realization.
Preserve explicit Function/Table operation authority for derived CRUD and cross-view diagnostics.
Represent Role, Task, TaskAction and explicit Function/I/O use while keeping human/manual work and target interaction separate.
Preserve business-flow nodes/lines as evidence-backed relations without assuming every Store/Ledger/Subject is canonical Data.
Preserve panel, spool, menu and layout information as target/presentation assets and visual evidence inputs.
candidateExtensions.authority: non-semantic unless an explicit semantic contribution is separately accepted

candidateExtensions.responsibility: Separate legacy Instance examples into Dataset, Snapshot, Scenario, Expectation and Presentation Order only when evidence supports the classification.
Preserve Script/LoginScript/shared functions and their dependencies/effects without treating executable code as semantic authority.
candidateExtensions.authority: runtime authority requires normal Capability/Permission/Resource bindings

candidateExtensions.responsibility: Map legacy special-table roles such as user/session/numbering/calendar/tax/exchange-rate services to explicit contracts and bindings.
candidateExtensions.authority: candidate semantics plus separate runtime/environment authority

rules: FormatVersion/Version are source metadata
Database/SMTP/credential/path/VM options are environment or realization inputs, never canonical business meaning
LoginScript/ScriptFunctions are native assets
special service table attributes are candidates for reference.xead.platform-service-binding
Remarks/Descriptions remain source prose unless separately accepted
ID is legacy source identity only
SortKey is ordering/import evidence only
membership and cross-subsystem operation diagnostics may be preserved without adding a Core Subsystem kind
Department is organization/context evidence and is not automatically an authorization role or Principal
legacy ID and SortKey remain source identity/order only
organization semantics require explicit acceptance before becoming reusable business meaning
legacy DataType can contribute scalar/domain semantics but does not become a Core type enum by name alone
format/options and physical representation remain distinct from accepted semantic type meaning
a Table may represent semantic Data, physical persistence, or a platform/runtime table; do not auto-promote every Table to domain Data
TableTypeID is legacy taxonomy evidence, not a Core enum
NATIVE/DERIVABLE/INHERITED are preserved as source facts
DERIVABLE does not establish derivation logic unless an accepted expression/evaluator can be traced
NoUpdate is interaction/policy pressure and is not automatically authorization
PK/FK/SK/XK and ordered TableKeyField membership are preserved as source-backed legacy key assertions
legacy PK or SK is not automatically a TEI business occurrence identifier or candidate key
legacy key membership does not by itself establish an accepted functional dependency
composite key shape does not by itself establish an allowed-combination/domain constraint; domain restriction is a separate semantic question
DDL realization evidence such as PRIMARY KEY or UNIQUE remains separate from business identity
FieldID and source ordering preserve membership in the enclosing legacy key
field position, name, type, or legacy ID is not canonical identity evidence
ambiguous or missing field resolution remains unresolved rather than being repaired by naming or type heuristics
Table1ID/TableKey1ID and Table2ID/TableKey2ID are source-backed relationship key references and remain distinct from business identity
key references may support explicit relation mapping only when the participating key fields resolve without ambiguity
FAMILY/REFFER/SUBTYPE meanings require lossless mapping or extension semantics
ExistWhen prose is not compiled into a constraint without explicit acceptance
XF/Menu/TableScript/custom type is an implementation/pattern hint, not canonical business identity
mapping to browse/record/header-detail/report/command or another pattern is a candidate decision, not a type alias
design Function is not assumed one-to-one with Xeaf executable Function
Parameters/Return prose is not a typed contract until explicitly modeled
Function call relations remain explicit source evidence
caller/callee usage is source-backed function dependency evidence
usage relation does not by itself establish Business Procedure order, transaction scope, or runtime authority
OpC/OpR/OpU/OpD is explicit Function/Table operation authority
CRUD matrix is derived and not a second source of truth
Function-level CRUD does not establish path-specific or Business Action-specific effect
panel text/layout is presentation evidence
panel identity may be referenced by a TaskFunctionIO but is not business action identity
report/spool layout remains presentation/native asset unless separate business semantics are explicitly accepted
Role is business actor/job context
do not convert it to authentication principal or authorization role
Task is a Business Procedure candidate
Event is business trigger/timing prose and not runtime scheduler configuration
manual/external action remains valid without a Function
ExecuteIf is source condition prose unless accepted as a deterministic constraint
missing ID requires source-locator/addressability handling; SortKey is not durable identity
FunctionID/IOID is explicit use evidence
Operations is target-specific interaction instruction and is separated from Business Action meaning
IOID in the benchmark addresses Panel/Spool; it does not itself establish Table effect
boundary position/size is presentation metadata
subject area may group flow meaning but is not canonical identity by default
Process may resolve to Task
Ledger/Store/Folder/Subject is not automatically semantic Data or Database state
SlideNumber is presentation/scenario evidence, not lifecycle authority
direction and endpoints are source flow evidence
line labels do not create data contracts or handoff authority by name alone
free text is preserved as source asset
SortKey can indicate time or explanation order and is not assumed to be a transition sequence
credentials/endpoints/paths remain environment or secret inputs
LoginScript/ScriptFunctions are native assets
special-table roles become explicit service contracts/bindings if accepted
runtime Subsystem grouping may correspond to design grouping but is not assumed identical
runtime grouping is not deployment, security, or canonical ownership authority by itself
runtime Table is realization evidence and does not replace accepted Data meaning
Key and Refer children are preserved separately as runtime mapping facts
physical/runtime table identity is not business occurrence identity
Type selects legacy Driver realization family
executable Function is not assumed identical to design Function
TimerOption is runtime scheduling and is distinct from Business trigger
KeyFields is a Function/Detail record-selection key; when absent the legacy Driver may fall back to the target Table PK, so selection key and Data identity must remain separate
native code remains authoritative only for its native behavior, not canonical meaning
semantic validation/derivation, persistence effect and presentation effect are extracted separately if accepted
static analysis is evidence, not effect authority
runtime field definition may realize Data/Relation meaning but does not replace the semantic source
editable/color/default/display behavior stays target/interaction-specific unless separately accepted
column order/width/rendering is projection metadata
button event may invoke a Function/Script but button label/action is not canonical Business Action by itself
filter definition is interaction/query realization evidence
filter fields or defaults do not create semantic constraints by themselves
ToTable/ToKeyFields/WithKeyFields are runtime reference mapping facts
empty ToKeyFields may be resolved by the legacy Driver through target-table PK fallback; that fallback is runtime behavior, not business identity
runtime refer mapping is not semantic Relation authority until reconciled and accepted
Detail describes a runtime interaction/table detail configuration
Detail KeyFields is a record-selection requirement and not Data identity
detail realization does not imply a distinct Business Action or canonical aggregate boundary
Type/Fields are runtime key realization facts
runtime PK is not business occurrence identity or functional-dependency authority
design TableKey and runtime Key must be reconciled through explicit source mapping rather than assumed equivalent
menu visibility/navigation is separated from business actor and authorization policy
